issue.title: AGW Bootstrapper Creates Unsupported P384 Client Certs

repository.name: magma
repository.description: Platform for building access networks and modular network services

issue.body:
### Your Environment

- **Version:** 1.1.0
- **Affected Component:** AGW
- **Affected Subcomponent:** magmad
- **Deployment Environment:** Any AGW deployment

### Describe the Issue

By default, magmad on the AGW will create a P384 curve private key as the challenge key for the gateway. When using this challenge key, the client cert and key received from a successful bootstrap procedure will use the P384 cipher.

If you try to use the `gateway.crt` and `gateway.key` client credentials in a direct (i.e. non-proxied) Python GRPC call to Orchestrator, the SSL handshake will always fail with `OPENSSL_internal:SSLV3_ALERT_ILLEGAL_PARAMETER`. `checkin_cli.py` will also incorrectly report that the SSL client certs are bad even though GRPC requests proxied through the local nghttpx reverse proxy will succeed.

**Expected behavior**

Direct GRPC connections to Orchestrator using bootstrapped client cert and key succeed.

**Additional context**

Switching to a P256 curve should fix this issue. GRPC doesn't support any other curves. See https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/23235

body: Ran into this issue today using python3-grpcio 1.30.2-3 on Debian Buster. In case anyone wonders, only the server/client certs need to be P256 curves, my P521 root and intermediate certificate authorities worked as is.
Is there any progress on this issue currently? In grpcio version 1.54.2, it still only permits the use of P256 elliptic curve client certificates.

issue.title: Allow more mtls curve
issue.body:
Due to the limitation of `python-grpcio`, which only supports the P256 elliptic curve(https://github.com/grpc/grpc/issues/23235), when AutoMTLS is enabled, the Python protocol plugin service cannot communicate properly with the Go Client.

Therefore, I have added the 'AutoMTLSCurve' option to allow specifying the curve type independently for AutoMTLS in the Client and Server. This will facilitate future extensions.
